review_notes: I read all of RadiusNormal.lean. It has three theorems and no simp attributes, simp sets or local simp lemmas. The proofs call `simpa using h` and `simp only [numericalRadius_zero, norm_zero]`. I checked `numericalRadius_zero` in Radius.lean, where it is tagged `@[simp]`, so the degenerate zero case is already covered. Possible `@[simp]` candidates are `numericalRadius_eq_norm_of_isStarNormal` and `numericalRadius_eq_norm_of_isSelfAdjoint`. The first would only fire when the `IsStarNormal` instance can be synthesised. The second has a non-instance hypothesis, so simp would have to discharge it. Rewriting `numericalRadius A` to `‖A‖` would also change a core quantity into a different one and could compete with other numerical-radius lemmas. I found no use in the supplied sources that needs that rewrite, so I did not recommend it. I did not find any cycle or competing rules, and I did not run Lean.
